FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 368
Committee: Economic Development and Tourism Sponsor: Representative Neil Rafferty
Analyst: Mathieu Fuller Date: 04/01/2024
House Bill 368 as introduced proposes a constitutional amendment, which if ratified, would
allow the Legislature to authorize the incorporation of innovation districts as public
corporations, the funding of innovation districts by the state and political subdivisions of the
state, the establishment of exemptions from certain laws of innovation districts, and to authorize
innovation districts to provide funding to other entities.
Further, this amendment would increase the proclamation expenses of the Governor, paid from
the State General Fund, by an estimated $100,000 for fiscal year 2025.
Page 1

FN-ZM6PRKR2
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 368
Committee: Economic Development and Tourism Sponsor: Representative Neil Rafferty
Analyst: Mathieu Fuller Date: 04/04/2024
House Bill 368 as reported by the Committee on Economic Development and Tourism proposes
a constitutional amendment, which if ratified, would allow the Legislature to authorize the
incorporation of innovation districts as public corporations, allows the Legislature to exempt
innovation districts by general law from certain constitutional provisions regarding debt and
granting of public funds, authorize innovation districts to provide funding to other entities, and
to provide that the financial obligations of an innovation district are exclusively the obligations
of the district.
Further, this amendment would increase the proclamation expenses of the Governor, paid from
the State General Fund, by an estimated $100,000 for fiscal year 2025.
